segments.text: This is a mathematics scratchpad. The working on screen is real, and half finished. It has never been submitted anywhere, so no server has ever seen it. An agent has just asked the page to check it, and the page has marked the first line that stopped being true. Line three. Nothing after it is marked, because everything after it follows from a mistake.
That verdict did not come from a language model. It came from a computer algebra system running inside the page.
This is the whole WebMCP surface. Eighteen tools, nine that read and nine that write, grouped so that an agent, or a person, can see its shape and its size without clicking anything.
These four matter most. An agent can differentiate, evaluate and compare against the page's own engine before it writes anything to a learner's work.

Now the agent repairs the line it broke, and finishes the answer. It is allowed to. This page used to refuse every agent write, and we withdrew the refusal, because a permission check in our own code never bound anything outside this page.

What replaces the refusal is on screen now. The round is closed, the unaided attempt is complete, and the page reports what it observed and who caused it. It also states what it does not establish. It does not claim anyone learned anything, and it says so in the same type size as everything else it claims.

And this is the part we are proudest of. Each of these seven verdicts was produced by executing the feature in this browser, just now. Three work. Two, origin scoping and cross origin reads, Chrome accepts and silently does not honour. We publish what the platform does not do.
